title: Aeolian Vocalion records and who played on them
summary: He explains the move to Aeolian over royalties, the playback incompatibility, and the lineup on the New York records.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Now I want to interrupt you again. These things are, to me, important to bring up. Now you made records for Victor and Columbia before you went.

Overseas, and Aeolian too. It was at this time that we had friction with Victor, that we went over to the Aeolian company. And we didn't know the Aeolian had a different soundtrack. We thought that they'd play on any machine. And we went over there on a royalty basis. That'd give us two cents a royalty, like they give Caruso and them, for the records. So we made several records for them. But when they found out, I think they had either the Hillingdale or the Laracut, I couldn't tell you. Because I don't know about these things. But you couldn't play them on a record phonograph. You had to get an expansion of something and people wouldn't buy the records. Therefore, that's when we went back to Victor again.
Well, I want to get clear. Who was in the band then, at that time, when you made the records for Aeolian?

All the records that were made in New York, the Aeolian, the Colombian, and the Victor, was the original band and types. Barbara, Shields, Ragus, and myself. And Edwards. That was the original Vixenland Jazz Band. All the masterpieces had been made before Edwards was drafted into the Army.
